title: Proofreading: Finding and Fixing Mistakes
summary: A simple checking routine for the last few minutes of the writing task, the mistakes to hunt for, tricky homophones and worked examples to practise on.

blocks.text: Proofreading means reading your writing again to **find and fix mistakes** in grammar, spelling and punctuation. Leave **the last 3–4 minutes** of your 30 minutes of writing time for it. Small mistakes that you can fix in seconds can cost marks in **Grammar and punctuation** (7 marks) and **Word structure (spelling)** (3 marks).
Check in this order. Read slowly, looking for **one kind of mistake at a time**.

items: **Sentences:** every sentence starts with a capital letter and ends with . ? or ! (no comma splices or run-ons).
**Tense:** the same main tense all the way through.
**Agreement:** we were, he doesn't, there are, everyone has.
**Standard English:** no we was, could of, me and him went.
**Punctuation:** commas in lists and after opening clauses, speech punctuated correctly, apostrophes in the right place (its/it's, their/they're/there).
**Spelling:** check tricky words, especially irregular past forms and -er/-est spellings.

blocks.title: Read it in your head, slowly
blocks.text: Point at each word with your pencil. If you read fast, your brain reads what you **meant** to write, not what is on the page.

items: Draw **one neat line** through the wrong word and write the correct one above it.
To add a missing word, put a small **^** and write the word above.
To show a new paragraph you forgot, write **//** before the sentence.
Do not scribble over words: the examiner must be able to read your work.

rows: Comma splice (two sentences joined by a comma)
It was late, we went home.
It was late, **so** we went home. / It was late. We went home.
She opened the box and finds a key.
She opened the box and **found** a key.
I bought three **apples**. (plurals do not need apostrophes)

blocks.text: 5. Homophones: words that sound the same

rows: a place / belongs to them / they are
They're putting their bags over there.
belongs to it / it is (or it has)
It's sad that the bird hurt its wing.
You're going to love your present.
towards / also or more than enough / 2
Two of us went to the shop too.
a place / past of are / put on clothes
Where were you going to wear that?
Who's the boy whose dog ran away?
A piece of cake fell off the plate.

blocks.text: This original paragraph has **at least ten** mistakes. Try to find them before you look at the correction.
last saturday me and my cousin goes to the zoo, we was very excited. The lions was sleeping but the monkeys were the most funniest animals there. Their was a sign that said “dont feed the animals.”

**Corrected:** Last Saturday, my cousin and I went to the zoo. We were very excited. The lions were sleeping, but the monkeys were the funniest animals there. There was a sign that said, “Don't feed the animals.”

items: last → Last (capital at the start of a sentence)
saturday → Saturday (days need capitals)
me and my cousin → my cousin and I (standard English)
goes → went (past tense)
zoo, we → zoo. We (comma splice fixed)
we was → we were (agreement)
The lions was → The lions were (agreement)
the most funniest → the funniest (double superlative)
Their was → There was (homophone)
dont feed → Don't feed (apostrophe for omission, and a capital letter at the start of the speech)
said “ → said, “ (a comma before the speech)

blocks.title: Where proofreading matters
items: **Writing:** there is no separate mark for checking, but every mistake you fix improves your **Grammar and punctuation** and **Word structure (spelling)** marks.

**Reading:** grammar and punctuation questions may ask you to spot or correct an error, choose the correct word (their/there), or explain why a punctuation mark is used. The same checking eye helps you there.

blocks.title: Know your own mistakes
blocks.text: Look at your last three pieces of marked writing. Write down the **two mistakes you make most** (for example we was or missing full stops). In the exam, hunt for those two first.

blocks.title: نصيحة سريعة
items: سيب آخر 3 أو 4 دقايق من وقت الكتابة للمراجعة، وما تكتبش لحد آخر ثانية.
راجع حاجة واحدة كل مرة: الحروف الكبيرة والنقط، بعدين الزمن، بعدين توافق الفاعل مع الفعل، بعدين الإملاء.
صلّح بخط واحد نضيف فوق الكلمة الغلط، ما تشخبطش.

items.q: Correct the sentence: my freind and me goes to the park every friday.
items.a: My **friend** and **I** **go** to the park every **Friday**. (capital letters, spelling of friend, standard English, agreement)

items.q: Fix the comma splice: The rain stopped, the children ran outside.
items.a: The rain stopped, **and** the children ran outside. / When the rain stopped, the children ran outside. / The rain stopped. The children ran outside.

items.q: Choose the right words: (Their / There / They're) going to visit (their / there / they're) grandmother.
Correct: The dog wagged it's tail.
items.a: The dog wagged **its** tail. (its = belonging to it; no apostrophe)

items.q: Find and fix the tense mistake: I picked up the phone and hear a strange voice.
Correct: I have two sister's and three brother's.
items.a: I have two **sisters** and three **brothers**. (plurals, no apostrophes)

items.q: Correct: Where you at the match yesterday? I seen you there.
items.a: **Were** you at the match yesterday? I **saw** you there.

items.q: Find and fix six mistakes:yesterday we visit the museum. it was more better than i expected, and the guide were very friendly.
items.a: Yesterday we **visited** the museum. **It** was **better** than **I** expected, and the guide **was** very friendly. (capital Yesterday, past tense visited, capital It, better not more better, capital I, guide was)

items.q: Why is it a good idea to proofread for one kind of mistake at a time?
items.a: Because your eyes look for one thing carefully instead of reading quickly and missing errors.
